title: Induction and finite histories in Peano arithmetic

based_on.title: Provability logic: models within models in Peano Arithmetic
An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Induction inside arithmetic constructs coded histories at every internal length.
abstract: To prove that a computation works for every input, arithmetic needs to reason about its intermediate values. Peano arithmetic can encode a finite history and prove that one more value can be appended without changing earlier entries. The key is to state the induction hypothesis as an arithmetic formula, allowing parameters to remain fixed throughout the argument. We develop the arithmetic needed for this construction and show how to collect witnesses for every index below a given bound into one code. These are uniform proofs inside the system, so they apply in nonstandard models too, where an ordinary externally finite list is not enough.
